children: is expanding its technology operations in India, with plans to create a global capability center in Chennai and employ about 800 technology workers, according to the Tamil Nadu government.
The company has entered into an agreement with the southern Indian state for the center. The government did not provide details on the planned investment.

Chennai, a major technology center in southern India, already hosts global operations for companies such as Citi, Barclays, and American Express. The city represents about 10% of the global capability centers operating in India, the state government said.

technology chief Anand Varadarajan cited the availability of skilled workers, lower employee attrition, and infrastructure as factors supporting the company’s decision, according to a state government release.
The move comes shortly after Walgreens agreed to establish a technology center in Chennai that is expected to create 250 jobs, according to a separate Reuters report.

has around 500 stores in India through its joint venture with the Tata Group. India had more than 2,100 global capability centers employing about 2.36 million people and generating nearly $100 billion in revenue, according to a 2026 Nasscom-Zinnov report. Such centers increasingly handle functions including finance, software development, and research and development.

title: Starbucks to build India technology hub in Chennai, target 800 hires
